name: NIST Heat Transmission Properties of Insulating and Building Materials (SRD 81)
description: Historical guarded-hot-plate measurements of building and insulating materials with specimen, apparatus and conditioning metadata; public JSON API.
version: Web version 2.0 (December 2015); data content last updated 1983
count_scope: Complete response from documented TableAllData endpoint retrieved 2026-11-01; one distinct database id per object
license: Database states copyright U.S. Department of Commerce, all rights reserved; no open data redistribution license verified

sources.title: SRD 81 live public JSON API
sources.evidence: Downloaded 2,175 objects with 2,175 distinct id values. Fields include material/manufacturer, specimen, density, thickness, mean temperature, temperature difference, conductivity, uncertainty, apparatus, method and conditioning; 1,667 rows have null unc.

sources.title: SRD 81 scope and measurement method
sources.evidence: Describes historical 200-mm guarded-hot-plate measurements, over 2,000 observations, most near 24 °C, with broad specimen-density coverage.

sources.title: SRD 81 definitions and uncertainty
sources.evidence: Defines SI/IP property units, specimen and pre-test conditions, apparatus and test mode; describes relative expanded uncertainty conventions. API numeric fields do not embed units.

sources.title: SRD 81 release history
sources.evidence: Web version 2.0 released December 2015, superseding version 1.0 released January 2000.

sources.title: SRD 81 landing page and rights
sources.evidence: Current public page identifies data content last updated 1983 and copyright U.S. Department of Commerce with all rights reserved.

caveats: 2,175 counts measurement rows, not distinct materials or specimens; API snapshot was checked 2026-11-01.
API fields do not encode units. Values appear to use inch-pound conventions; confirm each unit/conversion against the UI before quantitative reuse, and do not label API values SI by default.
1,667 of 2,175 API rows have null uncertainty. Provider default uncertainty guidance does not supply measured row-specific uncertainty.
Apparent thermal transmission properties can combine conduction, radiation and convection; they are not intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity.
Historical data content ends in 1983; current site accessibility and the 2015 software release are separate from measurement freshness.
Public access does not establish an open redistribution license.

name: NIST Cryogenic Materials Property Database
description: Temperature-dependent engineering-material property correlations, explicit fit coefficients and usable ranges, with a regenerator heat-capacity table.
version: Current TRC-hosted collection, checked 2026-11-01; individual revisions vary
count_scope: Public collection; total record count not verified
license: No collection-specific open data redistribution license verified

sources.title: NIST authoritative relocation notice
sources.evidence: Official NIST page explicitly moves the collection to the TRC materials-property index, preserving identity of the attached legacy database.

sources.title: 6061-T6 aluminum correlation tables
sources.evidence: Retrievable HTML tables provide coefficients, equations, property units, kelvin temperature ranges and fit errors for four properties; conductivity and specific heat have stated data ranges 4–300 K.

sources.title: Cryogenic property source bibliography
sources.evidence: Material-specific references supply literature provenance, including an Al6061 section.

sources.title: Regenerator material numerical table
sources.evidence: Retrievable spreadsheet-style HTML contains temperature-dependent volumetric heat capacities, with K and J/cm3-K labels.

caveats: Correlations fitted to compiled data are not independent raw measurements; fit error relative to data is not measurement uncertainty.
No verified complete bulk export or homogeneous release version; retrievable numerical tables are HTML, and individual material/property coverage varies.
The regenerator link returns spreadsheet-style HTML, not a verified standalone XLS/CSV file.
Index links and sampled data tables were verified; an exhaustive material, coefficient or measurement count was not established.
Respect each material, temper, orientation and equation-validity range; do not extrapolate fits beyond their stated ranges.
Public access does not establish an open redistribution license.

name: NIST Structural Ceramics Database (SRD 30)
description: Literature-derived ceramic property tables linked to processing, composition, measurement methods, evaluation status and bibliography.
version: Live Ceramics Data Portal; data content last updated 2002
count_scope: Public collection; total record count not verified
license: Database states copyright U.S. Department of Commerce, all rights reserved; no open data redistribution license verified

sources.title: WebSCD database and evaluation criteria
sources.evidence: Public search page identifies last data update 2002, ceramic families and evaluation criteria; it documents processing/composition and bibliography support.

sources.title: SCD citation Y00001 numerical record
sources.evidence: Live HTML record contains corundum heat-capacity values with K and J kg−1 K−1 units, value uncertainties, calorimetry methods, processing notes, source citation and property-specific evaluation labels.

sources.title: Current structural-ceramics search results
sources.evidence: Unfiltered search returns a linked citation index. Repeated citations can represent different materials; row or citation totals are not a unique-material count.

caveats: No verified complete structured bulk export or dataset cardinality; numerical per-citation HTML tables are publicly retrievable.
Evaluation labels are property-specific: the sampled record marks heat capacity evaluated and grain size unevaluated. Do not label all values validated.
Legacy data content last updated 2002; catalog/site timestamps do not indicate new measurements.
Contains literature data and may overlap NIST Property Data Summaries and other compilations.
Public access does not establish an open redistribution license.
